headline_marked: [[2 Bangladeshis killed]] and 24 injured in Riyadh airport missile attack
headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed and 24 injured in Riyadh airport missile attack
summary: A missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed two Bangladeshis and injured 24 others, disrupting flights and stranding hundreds.
details: A missile struck Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 10, killing two Bangladeshis and injuring 24 others. The victims included 11 workers and 13 Umrah pilgrims. The attack, which occurred around 3:15 AM local time, also resulted in the deaths of 10 others and injuries to 309 people of various nationalities.

The two deceased Bangladeshis have been identified as Shahed Ahmed from Bogura and Nasrullah Badrpuri from Cumilla. Three injured individuals are currently in the intensive care unit (ICU) at King Abdullah Hospital, with their conditions stable.

Among those in the ICU are Hafez Hasan (Dhaka), Kazi Nurullah (Brahmanbaria), and Omar Faruk (a Saudi-based worker). National Guard Hospital is treating Safat Rahman (Naogaon), who is unconscious, and Daudul Islam (Cumilla). Riyadh Medical Hospital is caring for Saimul Islam Saurav and Abul Mansur Md. Riyaz Uddin, both from Dhaka.

Further casualties are being treated at Prince Sultan Military Hospital, Kingdom Hospital, King Fahad Medical City, Prince Mohammad Bin Abdulaziz Hospital, Ester Sonad Hospital, and Sulaiman Alhabib Hospital. The embassy is coordinating medical care and providing updates on the condition of the injured.

The attack caused significant disruption to flights, stranding approximately 500 passengers who were either arriving from Bangladesh or awaiting onward international and domestic connections. The embassy has arranged accommodation and food for those affected, including 100 passengers from cancelled Saudia, Riyadh Air, and US-Bangla flights.

Special arrangements were made for 67 individuals who had arrived from Bangladesh in Ihram attire for Umrah, facilitating their transport to Jeddah. Additionally, around 400 passengers from a cancelled Saudia flight to Dhaka are being rerouted from Dammam's King Fahad International Airport. Two Bangladeshi workers were also assisted in crossing the border to Bahrain.

headline_marked: [[Charges framed]] over July killings of 11, including water distributor Mugdho
headline: Charges framed over July killings of 11, including water distributor Mugdho
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has framed charges against 26 people for the killing of 11 people during the July uprising. Families seek justice for their loved ones, including Mir Mahfuzur Rahman Mugdho, who was shot dead while distributing water to prot
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has framed charges against 26 individuals in connection with the killings of 11 people in Dhaka's Uttara on July 18 and 19, 2024. The charges include crimes against humanity, stemming from allegations of indiscriminate firing on unarmed protesters by police, senior officials, local Awami League leaders, and armed party activists.

Among the victims was ride-sharing driver Mokhlesur Rahman Durjoy, who was allegedly killed by an armoured personnel carrier. His body was reportedly kept at Uttara East Police Station before being disposed of in the Turag River to conceal the crime.

The prosecution alleges that former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former police chief Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun, and other senior officials orchestrated the crackdown under orders from the then prime minister to suppress the uprising. Eight accused were present during the charge framing, while 18 remain absconding.

For the family of Mir Mahfuzur Rahman Mugdho, who gained recognition for distributing water to protesters before being shot dead, birthdays are now painful reminders. His brother, Mir Mahmudur Rahman Dipto, expressed that the charge framing is a step towards justice, but the family's grief remains profound.

Mugdho's mother has struggled to cope with his death, unable to celebrate birthdays even for his twin brother, Snigdho. The family continues to mourn the loss of Mugdho, whose absence has irrevocably changed their lives.
The tribunal has scheduled November 4 for the prosecution's opening statement and the testimony of its first witness, marking the commencement of the trial.
